 ORDER

This writ petition is filed by petitioner - Smt. Neelu Sen W/o Shri Ashendra Sen, a victim of crime,
where allegation is that respondent No.5 raped her, being aggrieved of the order Annexure P-11 passed by the Executive Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Nagod, revoking suspension of respondent No.5 - Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen, Lineman,
Employee Code No.90534859 on 27.09.2023.

2. Petitioner's contention is that Annexure P-10 is a communication made from the office of the Superintending Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.,
Satna vide dispatch No.053- 95/Sama-06/2656 dated 27.09.2023, asking the Executive Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Nagod to revoke suspension of the respondent No.5 - Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen, in view of the stay granted by the High Court on 23.09.2023.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. It has come on record that the said order was never issued by the Superintending Engineer (O&M) but, was issued by the clerk, who was working in the office of the Superintending Engineer (O&M), namely, Shri A.N. Garg, represented by Shri Brijesh Kumar Choubey, learned counsel.

This fact is also admitted by Shri Mukesh Kumar Agrawal, learned counsel, appearing for respondents No.1 to 4.
4.

It is submitted that this letter was received in the office of Executive Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Nagod on 27.09.2023, as is evident from the seal which is affixed on Annexure P-10, showing inward No.892 dated 27.09.2023.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In pursuance of that order, though it is not referred in order Annexure P-11, private respondent's suspension was revoked.
5. It is pointed out that this High Court where W.P. No.23904/2023 was filed and was decided on 23.09.2023, there was no direction to stay the order of suspension.

It is only mentioned that:-
''Considering the aforesaid, present petition is disposed of with a direction to the appellate authority to take a decision on petitioner's appeal contained in Annexure P/7 as expeditiously as possible preferable within a period of sixty days from the date of production of certified copy of this order.''
Thus, it is evident that no stay was granted in favour of Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen S/o Shri Baijnath Sen, Lineman.

sentences.text: Shri Mukesh Kumar Agrawal, learned counsel appearing for the authorities of Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., in his turn, submits that order of revocation of suspension was passed on 27.09.2023 vide Annexure P-11 because petitioner therein Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen was to superannuate on 30.09.2023 and there were holidays during the intervening period.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Executive Engineer revoked the suspension on his own.
7. It is evident that Eid Milad-un-Nabi was on 28.09.2023 and 29.09.2023 and 30.09.2023 both were working days.

Thus, submission made by Shri Mukesh Kumar Agrawal, learned counsel that order was passed in view of the retirement of the respondent No.5 - Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen, is not made out from the record.

8. I have gone through the reply filed by the Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd. vide I.A. No.3026/2024, wherein there is no denial of the fact that unauthorized communication Annexure P-10 made by Shri A.N. Garg, clerk in the office of the Superintending Engineer on the letterhead of the Superintending Engineer, was received by the Executive Engineer (O&M) and Executive Engineer (O&M) though has cleverly not mentioned any reference to the same in the order Annexure P-11 but, he was acting in terms of that communication.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: There should have been a specific denial that communication Annexure P-10 was not received in the office of the Executive Engineer (O&M).
But there is none, even in the affidavit of the Executive Engineer.

9. Thus, it is apparent that the whole machinery of Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., which includes the then Superintending Engineer, whose name is not available and Executive Engineer (O&M) Shri K.K. Sethi were hand in glove with Shri A.N. Garg, clerk who was acting as the Incharge Section officer in the office of Superintending Engineer at the relevant point of time.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, action cannot stop only at Shri A.N. Garg, but the scope of enquiry will include Shri K.K. Sethi, Executive Engineer (O&M) and the then, Superintending Engineer, whose letterhead was misused and to whom an endorsement was made by Shri K.K.Sethi, as is evident from Annexure P-11.

This endorsement should have been taken note of by the Superintending Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Satna, had he not been hand in glove with the clerk and the Executive Engineer (O&M).

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
10. Submission made by Shri Mukesh Kumar Agrawal that the Executive Engineer Shri K.K. Sethi had revoked the suspension on his own in view of the retirement of Shri Sen on 30.09.2023, appears to be incorrect, inasmuch as, it is evident from the order dated 23.09.2023 passed in W.P.
No.23904/2023 that appeal against suspension was pending and admittedly, the Executive Engineer is not the appellate authority as the Executive Engineer had passed order of suspension on 04.07.2023.
11. High Court's order dated 23.09.2023 was passed by a coordinate Bench to decide the appeal in presence of learned Deputy Government Advocate.

12. Vide Annexure P-9, representation of the private respondent Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen addressed to the appellate authority was received in the office of the Executive Engineer vide inward Smt. Neelu Sen vs Managing Director on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35931614/
3 No.893 and bears endorsement of the Executive Engineer.

Thus, violating the orders of the High Court, the Executive Engineer could not have passed any orders on his own, but was obliged to refer the matter to the appellate authority i.e. the Superintending Engineer.

In this complete context,
communication made by a clerk of the Superintending Engineer as contained in Annexure P-10 attains significance.

When communications Annexure P-10 and Annexure P-9 are read in conjunction, then it is evident that since the Executive Engineer was in possession of the copy of the orders of the High Court as submitted to him vide Annexure P-9, he cleverly avoided any reference to Annexure P-10.

This prima facie shows his culpability and mens rea.
13.

It is also true that order of suspension, Annexure P-7, was passed on account of filing of the charge-sheet under Sections 376, 506, 509, IPC on 10.01.2023 and in compliance of the order of the Superintending Engineer's (Satna) letter No.053/95/07/1129 dated 04.07.2023.
Date of Annexure P-7 is also 04.07.2023.

Thus, there was no ground to revoke suspension by the Executive Engineer,
on his own, when he had issued order of suspension at the instance of the Superintending Engineer's communication and secondly, on criminal charge-sheet being filed.

14. Thus, it is evident that till this petition was filed in the year 2024, the authorities of the Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd. were never informed by the Superintending Engineer (O&M) to whom an endorsement was made in regard to order Annexure P-11, that he had never made any communication to the Executive Engineer and that Executive Engineer was not authorized to revoke the suspension as that would have come to an end automatically on the date of the superannuation.
15.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Shri Mukesh Kumar Agrawal, learned counsel has drawn attention of this Court to the affidavit filed in compliance of the order dated 04.03.2024 vide I.A. No.109/2024 to submit that in para 3 of the said affidavit duly supported with affidavits of Shri Krishna Kumar Sethi S/o Shri M.G. Sethi,
Executive Engineer, M.P.P.K.V.V.C.L.(O&M), Division - Nagod, Shri G.D. Tripathi, Retired Superintending Engineer, M.P.P.K.V.V.C.L.(O&M) Circle, Satna and Shri I.K. Tripathi, Chief Engineer, M.P.P.K.V.V.C.L., Rewa Division, Rewa

, it is mentioned as under:-
''That, it is humbly submitted that Executive Engineer has passed order dated 27/09/2023 (Pg 47 of WP) on its own in view of the fact that Shri Ghanshyam Sen was to retire on 29/09/2023.
Further, 28/09/2023 was a holiday.

Moreover, the order dated 27/09/2023, neither refers to the order of Superintending Engineer dated 27/09/2023 (Pg-46 of WP) nor order dated 23/09/2023 in WP No.
23904/2023 (P/8 with WP), thus, it is clear that there is no contempt by Executive Engineer as he passed the said order independent of order of SE or this Hon'ble Court.''
16.

An interesting aspect to the whole affidavit of the compliance is that the Executive Engineer, the Superintending Engineer or the Chief Engineer, have not bothered to refer to the fact that on Annexure P-10, communication made from the office of Superintending Engineer, though unauthorizedly by his clerk, there is an acknowledgement of the office of the Executive Engineer (O&M), Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Division Nagod, which was Smt. Neelu Sen vs Managing Director on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35931614/
4 received on 27.09.2023 vide inward No.892.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd., Division Nagod
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Vide inward No.893 dated 27.09.2023
, the Executive Engineer received copy of the orders of the High Court (Annexure P-9).

17. The pace at which the letter has travelled on the same day from Satna to Nagod and there being no denial of receiving that letter and then passing of the order Annexure P-11 on the same date i.e.
27.09.2023, there is a chain of connectivity prima facie reflecting the collusion between different functionaries of Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd. and the beneficiary Ghanshyam Prasad Sen.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Poorva Kshetra Vidyut Vitran Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
If the order was not passed keeping in mind the communication contained in Annexure P-10 then, the concerned Executive Engineer was required to show that this communication Annexure P- 10 was never received in his office on 27.09.2023 but, contrary is proved through the documentary evidence contained in Annexure P-9 and Annexure P- 10 which is not denied by the Executive Engineer.
18.

Merely, not mentioning the fact and giving reference of Annexure P-10 or that of the order of the High Court, will not absolve the Executive Engineer, inasmuch as, retirement date is not 29.09.2023 but 30.09.2023 and both the days i.e. 29.09.2023 and 30.09.2023 were working days and as mentioned above, there was no need to revoke the suspension as it would have come to an end with the retirement.
Thus, the affidavit which has been filed in compliance, is not satisfactory so to absolve the Executive Engineer and other functionaries of their liability.

19. As mentioned above, since there is a chain of events which prima facie reflects the involvement of all the functionaries to give illegal benefit to Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen, they have to face the consequences and that cannot be passed only on the clerk Shri A.N. Garg.
20.
Thus, the impugned order dated 27.09.2023 (Annexure P-11) is hereby quashed.

Departmental enquiry be instituted against Shri K.K. Sethi, Executive Engineer (O&M) and be conducted by an independent senior authority under the direct supervision of the CMD of the company and if need being, the FIR can also be filed against the Executive Engineer and other functionaries as has been filed against Shri A.N. Garg to complete the chain of events and also against the respondent No.5 - Shri Ghanshyam Prasad Sen, who was the ultimate beneficiary of the acts in passing orders Annexure P-10 and Annexure P-11.
21.
In above terms, this writ petition is allowed and disposed of.
